page: Microsoft Azure D32s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 128 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include a 480 MB L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 execution units, and cryptographic hardware support including AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes no bundled local disk storage and contains no discrete graphics hardware, requiring external remote block storage for persistence.

Performance metrics indicate strong compute and data processing capabilities. The instance achieved top-tier throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.79 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.35 GB/sec, alongside strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 226.88 GB/sec. PassMark testing reflects a strong CPU overall score of 53,875.1, bolstered by high encryption and physics calculation results. In network-facing benchmarks, static web serving throughput measured a strong 61.65 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing registered read-only throughput of 165.91 GB/sec and write throughput of 64.86 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks, while Redis operations maintained a mid-tier throughput of 60.05 million operations per second. In machine learning workloads, prompt processing across small and medium parameter models is accelerated by instruction extensions, whereas large-model generative token throughput demonstrates expected CPU architectural limits.

From a cost-efficiency and deployment perspective, the instance provides high compute density and modern instruction extensions for non-GPU environments. The absence of integrated ephemeral storage eliminates local disk overhead, allowing resource expenditure to align directly with compute and memory utilization while externalizing state to Premium Storage volumes. Microsoft Azure D32s_v7 is best fitted for high-concurrency web serving, compression and archive pipelines, microservices backends, continuous integration runners, and enterprise middleware.
description: Microsoft Azure D32s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz, paired with 128 GB of RAM and a 480 MB L3 cache. Featuring hardware support for Intel AMX, AVX-512, and advanced cryptography, the instance excels at high-throughput data processing, demonstrating top-tier compression and strong web serving throughput. It features no integrated local storage and no GPU acceleration, directing all persistence workloads toward network-attached Premium Storage. Memory bandwidth reaches 165.91 GB/sec on large read blocks, and CPU performance delivers strong results across multi-threaded physics, encryption, and prompt evaluation for small to medium language models. The platform offers balanced resource density and cost efficiency for enterprise application tiers, web serving clusters, batch compression routines, and backend enterprise software.
